findings: decode_str_items drops empty string elements. In valid JSON with call_log_shingles[0] empty and[1] nonempty, from_json shifts sketch1 to position0 instead of preserving positional association.

Original record/check control with equal1389-byte outputs: before JSON roundtrip a fuzzy query matches long-actual call2; after roundtrip it matches unrelated two-line call1 with actual shingle similarity0. This is a false candidate citation caused by storage misalignment, not a hash collision.
Python json independently validates saved complete context and confirms both original array positions; serialized bytes are not corrupt.

Legacy extract_str_array stops at the first closing bracket even inside a quoted item: a]b becomes a and remaining element is lost. The extract_all/map_str_array route preserves bracket-containing strings in the same control, while still dropping empty items.
Recursive parser converts a valid UTF-16 surrogate pair for U+1F600 into two U+FFFD replacements. It also accepts trailing non-JSON text and an unknown escape in finite controls.

Recursive numeric representation f64 rounds9007199254740993 to9007199254740992. Flat integer extractor preserves exact value. SessionContext uses flat integer extraction, so this is not evidence of hash-array numeric rounding there.
transfer_decision: Do not reuse these JSON extraction helpers or parallel-array persistence. Preserve empty positions, exact integer values and explicit record-to-fingerprint association. No foreign source copied into production.
